                                         1. Introduction                                                         Recent efforts have begun to extend vision-language
                                                                                                             models (VLMs) toward understanding 3D scenes. Early
                                         Vision-language models (VLMs) such as GPT-5, Gemini,                approaches, such as 3D-LLM [14], Cube-LLM [5], and
                                         and Qwen3-VL [2] have recently demonstrated remarkable              ShapeLLM [23], inject point-cloud or multi-view features
                                         ability in linking visual and textual information. They can         into 2D VLMs to improve geometric reasoning. While ef-
                                         describe scenes, answer questions, and reason composition-          fective in constrained settings, these methods depend heav-
                                         ally about image content without task-specific post-training.       ily on dense 3D supervision, curated datasets, or domain-
                                         Yet despite their impressive breadth, these models remain           specific architectures, limiting their scalability as general-
                                         fundamentally two-dimensional: they interpret the world             purpose models (Fig. 1(a)). Moreover, these training-based
                                         as projections rather than as volumetric, physical spaces.          methods can only be applied to open-sourced models, and
                                         Trained almost entirely on 2D images and 1D text [17],              cannot leverage the strong and ever-evolving proprietary
                                         they lack grounding and understanding in the inherently 3D          VLMs such as GPT-5. More recently, models like Mind-
                                         nature of the real world [37]. As a result, they struggle           Journey [39] and world models [38, 41] enrich 2D percep-
                                         with tasks that require genuine spatial understanding, such         tion with implicit 3D or temporal priors with video diffusion
                                         as reasoning under viewpoint changes, estimating relative           or generative modeling, but they still operate over 2D or se-
                                         positions, or predicting outcomes of object interactions [6].       quential representations. Consequently, even state-of-the-
                                         These limitations prevent current VLMs from achieving ro-           art VLMs struggle to achieve human-like spatial reasoning.

Figure 2. Overview of the SandboxVLM pipeline. Given an input image and a textual query, the system builds a compact, 3D-aware,
query-conditioned context for a vision-language model (VLM). A video diffusion prior first expands the input into a short multi-view
sequence along imagined trajectories guided by abstract control provided by the VLM. Inside the 3D Sandbox module, an off-the-shelf
depth estimator predicts per-frame depth and camera parameters, while the VLM identifies task-relevant objects that guide a 2D segmenter
to produce instance masks. The masked regions are lifted into coarse 3D proxies and merged across views through a Multi-View Voting
and Clustering step to form abstract 3D bounding boxes. Finally, informative renderings of these 3D abstractions are composed with the
query and fed back into the VLM for spatial and physical reasoning.

perspective change to enable perspective-aware reasoning               compact, 3D-aware, query-conditioned context for a VLM

approaches remain limited to 1D or 2D representations and              segmenter Sθ to produce masks {Mv,i } (Sec. 3.3). Masked

Sandbox. 3D Sandbox strikes a balance between informativeness
and interpretability, providing vivid spatial cues while filtering out                        In this work, we introduced SandboxVLM, a simple yet
irrelevant details.                                                                           powerful framework that equips vision-language models
                                                                                              with coarse 3D awareness through abstract perception.
ages. (8) outperforms (7) by 6.5%, indicating that addi-                                      Rather than relying on dense geometric reconstruction or
tional viewpoints provide crucial spatial cues that enhance                                   heavy supervision, our approach injects symbolic 3D struc-
the VLM’s reasoning capabilities. This highlights a gap                                       tures into existing VLMs via proxy elevation and multi-
in current generalist VLMs: they lack sufficient 3D spatial                                   view voting and clustering—allowing models to reason spa-
knowledge that generative world models inherently possess.                                    tially in a lightweight, training-free manner. Extensive ex-
The latter can therefore serve as a valuable source of 3D pri-                                periments across spatial reasoning benchmarks demonstrate
ors to complement VLMs, suggesting a promising direction                                      consistent and substantial gains over both generalist and
for future research.                                                                          training-based baselines, confirming that abstract 3D rep-
                                                                                              resentations can meaningfully enhance spatial intelligence.
(ii) Visual modality is not necessarily more informative

to VLMs than text. By comparing setting (2) with (3),

and (5) with (6), we find that for equivalent information

(iii) Providing 3D information to VLMs benefits spatial                                       age. While effective for many scenarios, this limits adapt-

representations. However, directly rendering point clouds                                     formation effectively, it does not explicitly model physical
(setting (4)) results in a substantial performance drop, even                                 properties such as mass, friction, or material characteris-

Table 4. Question types and examples from each benchmark. The four types of benchmarks we evaluated on contain various tasks
from metric questions like relative depths to comprehensive ones like physical scene understanding. For more details, please refer to the
corresponding paper.

   SAT Bench [25]
                    Ego Movement     How did the camera likely rotate when shooting the video?
               Object Movement       Were any of the objects in the initial frame that you can still see in the second frame moved from their original
                                     positions?
                        Goal Aim     I need to go to the houseplant. Which direction should I rotate to face it?
            Action Consequence       I need to go to the mirror (marked 1). If I turn left by 90 degrees, will I be facing away from the mirror?
                       Perspective   For someone at the x marked point and facing 90 degrees to the left, will the person surfing be to their left or
                                     right?
   BLINK [12]
                    Relative Depth   Which point is closer to the camera?
                 Spatial Relation    Is the bed at the right side of the dining table?
   EmbSpatial Bench [9]
                 Spatial Relation    How are statue and tissuebox positioned in relation to each other in the image? (multiple choices)
                                     A. The statue is at the left side of the tissuebox.
                                     B. The statue is touching the tissuebox.
                                     C. The statue is outside the tissuebox.
                                     D. The statue is right of the tissuebox.
   PhysBench [6]
        Physical Object Property     Which color of balls has the largest number?
                                     Given that the applied force is the same, which object in the images has higher stiffness?
    Physical Object Relationships    What is the distance between the yellow cube and the blue ball? (The blue cube has a width of 2 cm.)
                                     Which car has a higher average speed?
   Physical Scene Understanding      How does the focal length of the camera change?
                                     What causes the change in water level in the cup?
        Physical-based Dynamics      Which can is the ball most likely to land in?
                                     What is the correct sequence of images to make a gift box containing the perfume bottle?




Table 5. Composition of each ablation method. We list: Average: the average performance on SAT-Real [25]; Modality: in which modality
is the context information provided to VLM; Priors: whether a world model is used as a 3D-aware prior in generating the context; 3D:
whether the context is lifted into the 3D space; Filtered: before constructing the context, whether a VLM is used to collect information
relevant with the task; Using Boxes: whether we finally construct the 3D Sandbox as the context.

                  Were any of the objects in the initial frame that you can
                  still see in the second frame moved from their original
                  positions?
                  <think>I compare the initial egocentric image and the helper
                  (second) egocentric image: the same desk, monitors, cup,
                  and a small cardboard box near the trash bin are visible in
            (c.2) both frames. The rendered bird's-eye and step-back views for
                  t0 and t1 show the same object clusters with no relative
                  translations that would indicate an object was moved. The
                  imagined spin views of the corner with the cardboard box
                  also show the box in the same position relative to the bin and
                  desk. There is no evidence any visible object (including the
                  cardboard box) was shifted left or away from the camera
                  between frames. Therefore no object moved.</think>
                  <answer>no object moved</answer>
